record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: Can one develop new computational methods for solving periodic differential linear matrix inequalities arising in continuous-time periodic systems?

evidence.quote: New methods are also necessary for the solution of periodic differential LMIs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous-time linear periodic system on the real line, in which all coefficient matrices are continuous and T-periodic for some fixed period T>0. A periodic differential linear matrix inequality (PDLMI) on such a system is a constraint of the form

    F(t, X(t), \dot X(t)) \prec 0   for all t \in \mathbb{R},

where the unknown is a continuously differentiable, symmetric, T-periodic matrix-valued function X: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{S}^n (i.e. X(t+T) = X(t) and X(t)^\top = X(t)), and F is an affine map in (X, \dot X) whose coefficient matrices are continuous and T-periodic in t. A typical instance is the Lyapunov-type PDLMI

    A(t)^\top X(t) + X(t) A(t) + \dot X(t) + Q(t) \prec 0,   X(t+T) = X(t), X(t) \succ 0,

with continuous T-periodic A, Q.

Develop new computational methods (algorithms, with associated convergence and numerical reliability guarantees) for deciding feasibility of, and computing periodic solutions X(\cdot) to, general periodic differential linear matrix inequalities of the above type. In particular, design procedures that (i) handle the infinite-dimensional periodicity constraint without naive time gridding losing the periodic structure, (ii) exploit structural properties of the periodic coefficients (such as monodromy, characteristic multipliers, or representations via piecewise polynomial / Fourier / spline bases for X), and (iii) admit provable accuracy bounds on the computed X(\cdot) relative to the continuous PDLMI.
artifact.status_search_result: Several computational approaches to differential LMIs have appeared since the question was raised, including outer-linearization convex programming methods, piecewise-quadratic ansätze, and discretization-based reductions to standard LMI systems (e.g. Gershon-type and sampled-data DLMI methods, and the JOTA 2020 piecewise-polynomial scheme). These provide partial answers in the continuous-time and sometimes periodic setting, but a fully general, numerically reliable method for arbitrary periodic DLMIs with rigorous accuracy guarantees does not appear to be settled, so the broader problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the Numerical Solution of Differential Linear Matrix Inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Searches solutions in the class of piecewise-quadratic functions with symmetric matrix coefficients to be determined.
status_evidence.claim: A numerical method for DLMIs using piecewise-quadratic functions has been proposed, addressing part of the problem.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Methods for Solving Optimization Problems with Differential Linear Matrix Inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Optimization problems with DLMIs can be solved by discretization on the interval and reduction to interconnected LMIs at discrete time moments.
status_evidence.claim: Discretization-based numerical methods for DLMI optimization problems have been developed.

status_evidence.title: Differential linear matrix inequality in optimal sampled-data control
status_evidence.snippet: DLMI approach is introduced for the solution of various linear continuous-time control problems.
status_evidence.claim: DLMI-based computational frameworks for continuous-time control have been introduced.
